transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Um… mostly I’m just exhausted. Like, I came in because I’m so tired I can barely get through a shift. I’m a cashier, so it’s not like I’m running marathons or anything, but by halfway through it feels like my whole body is filled with wet sand.

And I’ll rest, or try to, but it doesn’t really bring me back. It’s weird, because I keep thinking maybe if I just sit down for a bit or get home and do nothing, I’ll feel normal again, but I don’t. I just stay… heavy. Like everything takes too much effort.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even things that you normally like doing?

Yeah… yeah, I have. It’s like, things I usually actually love just don’t land the same. I used to cook for myself and kind of make a whole thing of it, like music on, trying a new recipe… now it just feels like I’m moving food around because I’m supposed to eat.

And my guitar’s just sitting there. I’ll pick it up sometimes and then put it back down because it feels… flat, I guess. Same with hiking, or even going over to my family’s place. I know those are things I care about, but right now it feels like I’m pretending to care more than actually feeling it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. I’ve been low, I guess, but it kind of blends together with being tired, you know? Like yesterday at work this woman was arguing over coupons, and normally I’d just laugh it off later, but I just went home and sat on the couch staring at the wall.

So… most days, yeah, I feel kind of weighed down. But I’m not sure how to separate “down” from just feeling drained all the time.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like cooking, playing guitar, or spending time with family?

Yeah… that’s pretty much it. Cooking used to be this nice little thing for me, like I’d make a whole meal and feel proud of it, and now I’m just kind of standing in the kitchen thinking, why am I even doing this?

And guitar too. It’s sitting there, and I know I love it, or I used to, but when I pick it up it just feels flat. Same with hiking, going to see my family… I’ll go sometimes, but it feels like I’m acting normal, like I’m pretending to care or enjoy it more than I actually do.
Besides feeling tired and losing interest in things, have you also been feeling like you’re unable to shake a low mood, even when nothing specific is happening to make you feel that way?

I’m… not really sure. I mean, sometimes I’m just sitting there and I feel kind of heavy, but I don’t know if that’s a “low mood” or just me being worn out.

Like, I’ll be at the register and everything’s normal, people buying gum or cigarettes or whatever, and then I realize I haven’t really felt anything for hours. But then I start thinking about how the fluorescent lights in the store make everyone look sick, and then I’m wondering why they don’t change them because customers complain about everything else, you know?

So… I don’t know. I guess I can’t tell if I’m unable to shake it or if I’m just tired and spaced out.
Have you found yourself feeling slowed down, like even thinking is difficult, or have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Yeah… thinking does feel slow sometimes, like I’m trying to push through mud or something.

And the other part… I don’t like saying it, because it sounds dramatic, and I’m not trying to be dramatic. But I have had these scary thoughts, like maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. And a few times walking home, or near the road, I caught myself thinking about just… stepping off the curb into traffic.

Then I get freaked out, because I don’t really want to be thinking that. It just kind of shows up.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these feelings been going on for most days over the past couple of years?

Not a couple years, no… I don’t think so. The empty, low part has been more like… about four months now.

It’s weird because before that there was this burst where I had all this energy at work, like I was moving fast and getting things done, and I thought maybe I was just finally getting my act together. But after that passed, this other feeling just kind of stayed. Like the color got turned down on everything.

So yeah… most days lately, but not for years. More like these past few months.
Before these past four months, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I don’t really know. I mean, maybe? I’ve had bad stretches before, but I don’t remember if they were, like, two full weeks or just a few days that felt longer.

Time kind of blends together for me sometimes. Like when you work the same shifts and the same people come in every day, it’s hard to tell what was a whole “period” and what was just… a bad week. I used to think everyone just got like that sometimes.

So I can’t say for sure, no.
Before these past four months, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for a full two weeks or more?

I’m sorry, I know you just asked that and I’m kind of circling it. I honestly don’t know.

Like, I’ve had times before where I was down or didn’t really care about much, but whether it was a full two weeks… I can’t pin it down. My days kind of run together, especially with work and the same routine, and then later I’m like, was that two weeks or was that just a few rough days?

So I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. I can’t really remember a clear time like that before this.
Before these past four months, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for a full two weeks or more?

I’m not sure about before that, honestly. Like I said, I can’t really grab onto a clear two-week stretch from before.

What I do know is this low, empty part now has been going on about four months. It kept going even after that first rush of energy at work passed — like once that wore off, this stayed. Before that, I just… I don’t know if it was long enough to count or if I’m mixing up regular bad days with something bigger.
Before these past four months, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for a full two weeks or more?

I really don’t have a clean answer for that. I keep trying to think of one, like, some obvious stretch where I was down for two weeks straight, but it’s all kind of fuzzy.

There were times I didn’t feel like myself or I wasn’t excited about much, but then I start thinking about work schedules and weekends and whether I just hated a run of bad shifts, you know? Like, if I had a rude customer or money was tight, I’d be low, but I don’t know if that was the same thing you mean.

So… before these last four months, I can’t honestly say yes. I just don’t remember a clear full two weeks like that.
Before these past four months, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for a full two weeks or more?

Before these past four months, I can’t really say for sure. I keep thinking back and it gets messy.

What I do know is now, lately, things I normally love just feel… flat. Like cooking for myself used to be kind of my thing, and I’d play guitar or go hiking, or go over to my family’s place, and now I’ll do it or think about doing it and it feels like I’m pretending to care. Like I’m going through the motions.

Before this stretch, I don’t know if I had that for a full two weeks. I just can’t pin it down.
Before these past four months, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for a full two weeks or more?

I don’t know about before these four months, not clearly. I keep going back over it and it’s like… maybe there were times, but I can’t say it was a full two weeks.

What I can say is right now the stuff I usually love feels flat. Like cooking for myself used to make me feel normal, and I’d play guitar or go hiking, or stop by my family’s place, and now it’s like I’m doing the actions but not really feeling it. Like I’m pretending to care. Before this, though, I can’t pin down whether it happened like that for that long.
